paper.title: Dynamic Regret via Discounted-to-Dynamic Reduction with Applications to Curved Losses and Adam Optimizer
paper.anchor: Section 2.2, Theorem 1 (Modular D2D Reduction); proof in Appendix B.2

informal_statement: Theorem 1 gives a modular discounted-to-dynamic reduction converting a rescaled-regret bound into an explicit dynamic regret bound via stability terms Lambda_s and comparator variation.

exact_statement.quantifiers: for all T >= 1; for all beta in (0,1]; for all sequences f_1..f_T of functions on X; for all x_1..x_T in X; for all u_1..u_T in X; for all phi_1..phi_T and Lambda_1..Lambda_T
exact_statement.hypothesis_H: for every t in [T] and every u in X: sum_{s=1..t} beta^{-s} f_s(x_s) - sum_{s=1..t} beta^{-s} f_s(u) <= phi_t(u) + sum_{s=1..t} Lambda_s,  with Lambda_s >= 0 and phi_t(.) >= 0
exact_statement.conclusion_C: sum_{t=1..T} f_t(x_t) - sum_{t=1..T} f_t(u_t) <= beta*phi_1(u_1) + sum_{t=1..T} beta^t Lambda_t + beta*sum_{t=1..T-1} (F_t(u_{t+1}) - F_t(u_t)) + beta*sum_{t=1..T-1} beta^t (phi_{t+1}(u_{t+1}) - phi_t(u_{t+1}))

definitions.P_T^beta: sum_{t=1..T-1} sum_{s=0..t} p^beta_{t,s} [ f_s(u_{t+1}) - f_s(u_t) ]_+ with p^beta_{t,s} = beta^{t-s} / sum_{tau=0..t} beta^{t-tau}, f_0 := phi (used only in the corollary bounding the path term, not in Theorem 1 itself)

claim_type: universally quantified algebraic implication (not an empirical regularity)
what_would_falsify_it: a single instance (T, beta in (0,1], f, x, u, phi, Lambda) that satisfies hypothesis H at every t and every u, yet violates conclusion C

verification_design.primary: machine-checkable proof certificate: RHS(C) - LHS(C) == (1-beta) * sum_{t=1..T} S_t(u_t) + beta * S_T(u_T), where S_t(u) = beta^t phi_t(u) + beta^t sum_{s<=t} Lambda_s - Reg_{t;beta}(u) >= 0 is exactly hypothesis H. Certificate coefficients (1-beta) and beta are nonnegative precisely on the stated domain beta in [0,1], so the identity proves the theorem.
verification_design.route_a: exhaustive exact symbolic verification of the certificate identity for every T in [1,20] over free symbols with no numeric substitution
verification_design.route_b: general-T proof by coefficient matching: the identity is linear in its free symbols; the five symbol classes are enumerated exhaustively and each closed-form coefficient identity is verified symbolically with T, s, k free integer symbols. Routes A and B together cover all T >= 1.
verification_design.route_c: exact rational-arithmetic instance cross-check on 4000 randomly generated hypothesis-satisfying instances (fractions.Fraction; no floating point), guarding against a mis-transcription of the theorem statement
negative_controls: halve_phi1 - halve the beta*phi_1(u_1) term: certificate must break
drop_lambda - delete sum_t beta^t Lambda_t: certificate must break
drop_path - delete the F_t path term: certificate must break
drop_phidrift - delete the phi drift term: certificate must break
beta_squared_lambda - replace beta^t Lambda_t by beta^{2t} Lambda_t: certificate must break
hypothesis_only_at_T - assume H only at t=T rather than every t: an explicit counterexample to C must exist, proving the per-round hypothesis is load-bearing

non_circularity: The certificate is derived from the Appendix B.2 proof but is checked as an independent algebraic identity over free symbols; nothing about the data, horizon, or tolerance is chosen using the formula being tested. Route C generates instances from arbitrary rationals and then constructs phi to satisfy H, rather than constructing instances from the conclusion.
pass_condition: route A holds for every T in [1,20] AND route B holds for all five symbol classes AND route C reports zero violations AND every negative control breaks as designed
